Alex — thanks for the intro and the resume. I reviewed briefly and would like to run a compact 4-interviewer loop (90 minutes):

- 25m: System & production design (Laura) — end-to-end inference pipelines, scaling choices
- 20m: Model-serving performance & kernels (Marissa) — latency tradeoffs, batching, KV cache strategies
- 20m: Leadership & execution (me) — roadmap, cross-team rollouts, incident handling
- 25m: Deep debugging / coding exercise (Aditya) — small focused exercise on KV/cache behavior + follow-up discussion

Primary asks for the candidate: share any public repo or notes on performance tuning; be prepared to sketch latency vs cost tradeoffs and a recent example where they changed runtime to meet an SLO.

I’m attaching the interview choreography doc (senior-inference-interview-choreography.pdf) — includes question themes and leveling anchors. Please add Marissa to the loop and confirm availability windows.

If we need a bar-raiser / leveling anchor outside this group, propose one but I’d prefer we keep the loop tight.

Thanks,
Hiro Tanaka
Hiring Manager, Inference Runtime

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 10:03 AM Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I’m attaching the interview choreography doc (senior-inference-interview-choreography.pdf) — includes question themes and leveling anchors.

Thanks — I reviewed the doc and sketched a short leveling rubric to keep the panel consistent. High-level notes below that I’d like the panel to call out explicitly during debriefs.

Leveling anchors (Senior vs Staff):
- Senior: autonomous owner of a medium-sized inference stack; writes clear designs, ships reliable optimizations that reduce p50/p95; mentors peers.
- Staff: drives architecture across multiple services, sets kernel/quantization strategy, leads cross-org rollouts with measurable metrics improvement.

Interview focus suggestions (keep on the same language during debriefs):
- Production correctness: Does candidate proactively handle cache invalidation, rollout safety, and regression testing?
- Performance engineering: concrete examples of profiling, kernel selection, batching heuristics, and when to trade off latency for cost.
- Systems thinking: ability to reason about tail latency sources, multi-tenant isolation, and graceful degradation/fallbacks.
- Leadership: influencing without direct authority, prioritization under SLO pressure, handling postmortems.

Red flags to surface: vague answers about instrumenting latency, no examples of rollouts that reduced customer impact, inability to describe tradeoffs or benchmarking approach.

I’ll prepare 6 targeted questions for the kernels/perf slot and add a short rubric (score 1-4 with example anchors) to the choreography PDF.

Marissa
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Performance
Redwood Inference
